title: Teachers’ Experiences in Ensuring the Inclusion of Students with Special Needs in Primary Education
abstract: This qualitative research study aims to capture the attitudes of elementary school teachers regarding the inclusion of students with special needs in elementary education, the teachers’ knowledge of inclusive education as well as to analyze the strategies they use, the challenges they face, and their support needs during this process. To conduct this research, we used semi-structured interviews with 20 elementary school teachers. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify the main themes that emerged from the teachers’ responses. The results of this study show that teachers are committed to inclusion but face challenges such as a lack of resources and insufficient training. The study also considers the implications of inclusive practices in English Language Teaching (ELT), where learning a foreign language presents additional challenges for students with special educational needs.

title: Deciphering Masalili Weaving: An Ethnomathematical Approach to Enhance Mathematical Literacy in Southeast Sulawesi
abstract: The stagnation of mathematical literacy among students in regional Indonesia necessitates culturally resonant pedagogical interventions. This study examines the efficacy of integrating Masalili weaving, a traditional textile from Southeast Sulawesi, into the geometry curriculum to enhance mathematical literacy and student interest. Using a quasi-experimental design with a non-equivalent control group, 256 sixth-grade students were recruited. The experimental group received instruction via an ethnomathematics-based module, while the control group followed the conventional curriculum. Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) revealed a significant multivariate effect for the instructional method p

title: Rethinking Collaboration in Elementary Social Studies: Conceptual Understanding as the Missing Link in Learning Outcomes
abstract: Despite the widespread assumption that collaboration promotes higher-order thinking in elementary social studies, classroom evidence suggests its cognitive contribution is inconsistent. This study examines the structural roles of social studies conceptual understanding in predicting collaboration skills and learning outcomes among Grade V students. Using a quantitative explanatory design, data were collected from 200 students through questionnaires and essay-based assessments and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings show that conceptual understanding is not a homogeneous construct. Content Knowledge, Conceptual Integration, and Conceptual Application emerge as the strongest predictors of both collaboration skills and learning outcomes. In contrast, Collaboration Skill does not directly influence learning outcomes, while Social Case Analysis remains structurally peripheral. These results suggest that collaboration functions as a supportive pedagogical context rather than a direct cognitive mechanism, highlighting the central role of conceptual coherence in elementary social studies learning.

title: Epistemological Configurations and the Structural Positioning of Ethnography in Mixed-Methods Research
abstract: This research challenges the conventional understanding of mixed methods as primarily an integrative procedure and proposes to consider them from an epistemological-constructivist perspective. Based on a systematically collected and analyzed corpus of 35 peer-reviewed papers published between 2000 and 2025, the study examines how qualitative and quantitative research logics are interconnected, complementary, or remain in tension. The analytical framework encompasses paradigms of knowledge, the role of ethnography, patterns of integration, and relationships between different forms of cognition. The findings suggest that mixed methods do not represent a single methodological entity, but rather a set of distinct epistemological configurations. In particular, sequential asymmetry, parallel epistemological tension, and nested dependency are highlighted as patterns that shape the logic of research design. The proposed model of epistemological construction shows that tensions between different research traditions are not necessarily obstacles to integration but can represent a productive source of theoretical and methodological development of mixed methods. title: Exploring the Role of Communication Skills in the Relationship Between Reading Attentiveness and Cultural Literacy Among Pre-Service Elementary School Teachers: A Mediation and Moderation Analysis
abstract: This research investigates the roles of communication skills, reading attentiveness, and cultural literacy among pre-service elementary school teachers, with particular emphasis on how cultural literacy mediates and moderates the relationship between communication skills and reading attentiveness. Adopting an exploratory quantitative design, data were collected from 207 pre-service teachers across six Indonesian universities. Confirmatory factor analysis, mediation and moderation analyses, and ANCOVA were employed to analyze the data. The findings indicate that communication skills significantly influence cultural literacy and reading attentiveness. Cultural literacy, in turn, mediates and moderates the relationship between communication skills and reading attentiveness, with demographic variables such as age and geographical background also exerting significant effects. The results suggest the importance of integrating cultural literacy into teacher education programs, as it enhances both communication competence and reading engagement, thereby fostering more inclusive and effective teaching practices.

title: Empathy and Ethics in Aesthetic Surgery: Between Medical Responsibility and Socially Constructed Beauty Ideals
abstract: Objective. To analyze the ethical, psychological, and social dimensions of contemporary aesthetic surgery, with particular emphasis on empathy in clinical decision-making, patient autonomy, body image disturbance, and the risks associated with unregulated practice. Narrative review. This manuscript is based on a qualitative narrative review of the literature in plastic surgery, bioethics, psychology, and public health, including professional guidance documents and selected epidemiological reports. Available evidence was examined through the core principles of medical ethics: beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, and justice. Aesthetic surgery increasingly operates at the intersection of medicine, consumer culture, and digitally mediated beauty ideals. The literature indicates that requests for aesthetic procedures may be shaped by social media exposure, unrealistic expectations, and, in some patients, body dysmorphic disorder or other psychological vulnerabilities. Ethical practice, therefore, requires empathic communication, careful assessment of indications, and willingness to decline procedures that are unlikely to benefit the patient. title: Exploring the Experiences of Novice Teachers in Kosovo in the Process of Entering the Teaching Profession
abstract: This qualitative descriptive case study explored the experiences of novice teachers at the beginning of their teaching careers in Kosovo, focusing on their professional support, adaptation to school culture, and teaching practice in real classroom settings. The study also examined the perceived contribution of pre-service teacher education programs and the institutional support needed during the first year of teaching. Data were collected through interviews with 15 novice teachers and an analysis of official documents related to teacher development, supported by relevant literature. Findings revealed that schools in Kosovo generally lack formal induction programs and structured supervision systems for novice teachers. Participants reported varying support practices across schools, which often failed to address their professional needs. Consequently, novice teachers experienced challenges in adapting to school culture, lesson planning, and classroom instruction. The study highlights the importance of developing institutional induction programs and diverse support mechanisms to facilitate novice teachers’ professional growth and successful integration into the teaching profession.

title: The Use of AI in Students’ Research Work: The Attitudes of Professors from Faculties of Education
abstract: The purpose of this study is to gather the attitudes of professors from the Faculty of Education regarding their experiences with students’ use of artificial intelligence during research work. The study aims to identify the benefits, challenges, impacts on quality and academic integrity, ethics, privacy, perspectives, and the role of AI in the future of higher education. The research was conducted using a qualitative approach; the sample for this study is purposive, comprising a total of 20 university professors from Education Faculties in Kosovo. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, which allow flexibility in exploring key topics and enable participants to freely articulate their thoughts. Thematic analysis was used to identify and interpret the main patterns related to professors’ attitudes toward students’ use of AI. The study’s findings provide a clear insight into how university professors assess the impact of AI on the academic process, highlighting its potential to enhance learning, but also concerns about academic integrity and ethical use. The study emphasizes the need for clear institutional guidelines and policies that would enable sustainable, ethical

title: Technology and Inclusive Education: Opportunities and Challenges for Students with Special Educational Needs
abstract: This study investigates the role of technology in supporting inclusive education for students with special needs in lower secondary schools in Kosovo. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected through interviews with 26 students (15 from regular classes and 9 with special needs) and 9 parents. The findings show that technology enhances motivation, independent learning, collaboration, and active participation. Students reported frequently using tablets, computers, interactive applications, and multimedia resources, which enabled them to learn at their own pace and demonstrate their understanding more effectively. Students with special educational needs particularly emphasized the importance of simple, accessible, and visually supportive tools in building confidence and improving comprehension. However, challenges such as limited access to devices, technical difficulties, and insufficient teacher support were noted. Parents confirmed the benefits of technology but stressed the need for guidance and equal access. The study concludes that technology can strengthen inclusive education, provided that adequate resources and teacher training are ensured.

title: Baseline Assessment of Vocabulary Proficiency Among Teacher Trainees: Implications for Digital Storytelling Intervention
abstract: The present study seeks to understand the existing levels of vocabulary proficiency amongst teacher trainees, which will serve as a basis for future digital storytelling intervention. Vocabulary proficiency forms an important part of second language proficiency and is critical in ensuring pedagogic communication. The present research adopts a quantitative research design to study the various aspects of vocabulary knowledge, namely vocabulary size, polysemy, word associations, collocations, grammar behavior, and pragmatics. The sample consisted of 60 teacher trainees studying in integrated B.A. B.Ed. and B.Sc. B.Ed. programs offered in a university in Tamil Nadu, India. Data was collected from participants by means of a vocabulary test and analyzed using descriptive statistics. Results show that participants had moderate levels of vocabulary proficiency; however, they scored relatively high in vocabulary size but low in pragmatics. These findings suggest that the vocabulary proficiency of participants is multifaceted in nature, and specific weaknesses exist in terms of vocabulary use. Therefore, evidence-based digital storytelling interventions can be designed for improving vocabula

title: Media Representations of Disability and Their Impact on Social Inclusion and Rehabilitation Outcomes
abstract: The media plays an important role in how individuals in rehabilitation programs perceive themselves and their place in society. In this context, media representations of disability can directly influence the level of social inclusion and the motivation to engage in the rehabilitation process. Stereotypical or negative portrayals tend to reinforce feelings of stigmatization and isolation, hindering active participation, while realistic and empowering representations can contribute to increased self-confidence, social support, and positive recovery outcomes. This study examines how media representations affect social inclusion and rehabilitation among adults enrolled in rehabilitation programs. A mixed-methods design was applied. Quantitative data were collected through standardized questionnaires measuring media exposure, perceived stigma, social inclusion, and rehabilitation engagement. Qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews exploring personal experiences with media and its perceived impact on recovery. The sample included 150 adults participating in physical, vocational, or psychosocial rehabilitation programs in urban centers. Correlation and regression

title: Assessing Multidimensional Mathematical Learning: A Comparative Study of Alternative Assessment Tools in Teaching Functions
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of alternative assessment tools used in teaching functions in high school mathematics. The research was conducted with 54 tenth-grade students at GjonBuzuku Science High School in Kosovo during the 2024–2025 academic year, employing a quasi-experimental design. Within an active learning framework, worksheets, concept maps, structured grids, and poster presentations were implemented in the experimental group. Student performance was evaluated using analytical rubrics based on conceptual accuracy, representation, reasoning, and integrity. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, one-way ANOVA, and eta-squared (η²) effect sizes. Although no statistically significant differences were found in overall achievement scores, further analyses revealed educationally meaningful distinctions among the tools. Specifically, worksheets and structured grids were more effective in assessing procedural and conceptual accuracy, whereas concept maps better captured students’ relational understanding. In contrast, poster presentations showed relatively lower performance across most criteria. These findings suggest that using multiple assessment tools

title: AI Addiction: Exploring the Impact of ChatGPT Reliance on SelfRegulated Learning
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of students’ reliance on ChatGPT on their learning independence. Using a quantitative descriptive correlational design, the study involved 312 students from various academic programs who used ChatGPT in learning activities. The re- searchers collected data using questionnaires measuring ChatGPT dependency and self-reg- ulated learning, and analyzed them using Pearson’s correlation and simple linear regression. The results revealed a significant negative relationship between ChatGPT dependence and learning independence (r = −0.468, p

title: Scaffolding Academic Success: The Role of Instructor-Guided GPTs in Managing Task Complexity for Pre-Service Teachers
abstract: This study evaluates the instructional impact of Teacher’s Bag, an instructor-designed, context-aware custom GPT system, on pre-service teachers’ academic achievement. Utilizing a course-embedded quasi-experimental design at a Turkish public university, the research analyzed performance-based assessments in Curriculum Development and Educational Research Methods courses. The system provided pedagogically constrained, task-specific scaffolding aligned with national curricular objectives. Results revealed tasksensitive outcomes. In Curriculum Development, the AI functioned as a stabilizing scaffold, maintaining performance despite significantly increased final task complexity. In Educational Research Methods, the system enabled students to navigate a major transition from quantitative to mixed-methods designs, though accompanied by lower mean scores reflecting heightened cognitive demand. These findings challenge the “AI as a shortcut” narrative, demonstrating that pedagogically designed AI supports meaningful engagement with complex tasks without artificial grade inflation.

title: Attitudes of Kindergarten Teachers on the Integration of Children with Special Needs in Kindergartens
abstract: Children with special needs require appropriate support from families, teachers, educational institutions, and society. In Kosovo, despite efforts by the Ministry of Education and various organizations to promote inclusion, many children with special needs still have limited access to early education. This study examines kindergarten teachers’ attitudes toward the inclusion of children with special needs in preschool settings. A quantitative descriptive research design was employed, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using statistical procedures. The findings indicate that professional development has a moderate impact on teachers’ attitudes and highlight the need for continuous training, particularly in supporting children with disabilities and behavioral challenges.

title: Fostering Learning and Innovative Behavior in Adult Learners Through Learning and Innovation Platforms
abstract: Transforming local communities to foster sustainable careers for adults through the development of community-driven innovations presents a challenge in this era. This study examines the enhancement and development of community innovation through the Learning and Innovation Platform (LIP), and to investigates the innovative behavior of community members who were developed through the LIP. Participants consisted of 64 community members selected through volunteer sampling. The LIP, including 4 activities, was employed to enhance and develop community innovation and innovative behavior. Utilizing a quasiexperimental one-group design with the multi-measurement. The Community Innovative Behavior Scale (CIBS) was used to measure innovative behavior. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze the innovative behavior. Repeated measures ANOVA was conducted to evaluate the mean differences in innovative behavior scores, with pairwise comparisons performed using the Bonferroni post hoc test. The results revealed that the community innovation product was germinated brown rice powder packaged in sachets, recognized as a healthy product with excellent nutritional benefits. title: Mapping Global Trends in Higher Education Admission Strategies Over the Last Decade: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: This study examines global trends and thematic developments in research on higher education student admission strategies from 2016 to 2025, amid increasingly complex selection policies and expanding digital influence. Using a bibliometric analysis of 487 Scopus-indexed documents, metadata were refined with OpenRefine and analyzed using Biblioshiny R and VOSviewer to map publication patterns, collaborations, and keyword networks. Results show a significant rise in publications since 2018, peaking in 2024. Leading sources include Academic Medicine and ASEE Annual Conference Proceedings, with prominent contributors such as Glazer, James-Maceachern, Nesterov, and Sin. Five main thematic clusters emerged: student recruitment policy, professional education, cultural diversity, educational psychology, and academic evaluation. Emerging topics include machine learning applications, sustainability-oriented admissions, and digital justice. These developments highlight the growing need to integrate technological innovation with social equity to promote inclusive and transparent global admission practices.

title: The Historical Role of Global Diplomacy in the Development of Educational Technologies for Education and Rehabilitation
abstract: This paper critically analyzes the history underlying the role of global diplomacy in the development and spread of educational technology in the areas of education and rehabilitation. Since World War II, global cooperation among nations, global bodies, and educational systems has been important in influencing global educational systems through technological development. Through historical analysis, the paper seeks to investigate the role that global diplomacy has played in influencing the development of educational technology, such as online learning environments and technology-driven rehabilitation processes. Through a mixed research study methods that gathers data from a questionnaire survey among 42 respondents aimed at reviewing the effectiveness of educational technology in learning processes and rehabilitation programs, the paper finds conclusive evidence that technology-driven educational processes have played a positively significant role in influencing engagement in learning processes, thereby suggesting that global diplomacy is a useful tool in achieving equal educational access among all through the proper development of educational technology.

title: General Education School Experiences of Individuals with Visual Impairments
abstract: This qualitative study examines the dual nature of inclusion to uncover the negative challenges students encounter and the factors that alleviate these barriers to promote positive outcomes. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven adults (six women, one man) possessing congenital visual impairments (VI) who participated in general education classrooms during portions of their primary and secondary education. The data were analyzed utilizing a six-phase thematic analysis process. Four overarching themes that reflect participants’ accounts were identified, namely, (1) pervasive peer bullying, (2) refusing assistive devices, (3) lack of appropriate accommodations, and (4) factors contributing to positive experiences. Notwithstanding significant social trauma and institutional neglect, all participants attained advanced academic milestones, facilitated by self-advocacy, extracurricular engagement, and supportive educators. To convert policy into equitable practice, educational institutions must proactively foster inclusive settings by normalizing assistive technology, imposing stringent anti-bullying measures, and equipping general educators with specialized training to ap

title: Influences on Educational and Career Choice: Examining Career Guidance Exposure among Indian Science and Technology Students
abstract: Indian students increasingly enroll in STEM courses after senior secondary education, both within India and abroad. But the reasons behind such enrolment decisions are unfortunately not always clear. At the same time, students’ ideas about Arts and Humanities disciplines are unclear and not well defined. The present study examines the factors influencing students’ educational and career choices, with particular attention to the role of social agents. The core objectives are to identify the elements shaping students’ decisions, evaluate their exposure to various academic streams and career counselling sessions, and assess their awareness of opportunities within the arts, humanities, and social sciences. To address these objectives, a quantitative research design was employed, involving a sample of 525 participants currently enrolled in science and technology programs. The majority of the participants had completed their education in private senior secondary schools in Tamil Nadu, India. The findings reveal that social agents play a significant role in directing students’ educational and career trajectories. Moreover, the participants underscored the limited availability of career gu

title: Psychosocial Rehabilitation of Children with Sensory Disabilities in India: A Comprehensive Thematic Review of Family and Maternal Interventions
abstract: Sensory impairments affect millions of children in India. Family-centred approaches have been acknowledged as effective for psychosocial rehabilitation in this regard. This comprehensive thematic review synthesises evidence regarding family and maternal interventions for the psychosocial rehabilitation of children with sensory disabilities in India. A systematic search across six databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, Google Scholar, and CINAHL) resulted in studies published from 2010 to 2025. Children aged 0–12 years with visual or hearing impairments who are supported by their families are included in the study. Braun and Clarke’s six-phase approach was employed for conducting thematic analysis. An analysis of 40 studies revealed seven themes: (1) Family-centred intervention models, (2) Maternal Mental Health and Coping, (3) Sibling and Extended Family involvement, (4) Community-based Rehabilitation, (5) Cultural and Socioeconomic Factors, (6) Educational Integration, and (7) Barriers to accessing services. Family-centred interventions show significant promise. Significant gaps remain in providing maternal mental health support and services, and culturally adapted i

title: The Optimizing Students’ Mathematical Diversity: Differentiated Instruction Model on Students’ Mathematical Thinking
abstract: Mathematical thinking, which involves high-level logic, analysis, connections, problemsolving, and communication, is essential for navigating 21st-century developments. This study examines the impact of a differentiated instruction model on students’ mathematical thinking. A quantitative study adopting a predictive correlational design was conducted with a total of 105 elementary school students in the fourth grade in Riau Province, Indonesia. This study was analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS 4 software. The findings reveal that differentiated instruction for students to explore, discover, and experiment in building has a significant impact on students’ mathematical thinking, namely: mathematical communication, mathematical representation, mathematical problem-solving, and mathematical reasoning. Differentiated instruction can optimize the improvement of each student’s mathematical thinking diversity from an early age as a provision for elementary school students, as it can accommodate various potential differences for the sake of developing and optimizing competencies.

title: Professional Development of Preschool Educators: An Analysis of Contemporary Needs and Challenges
abstract: An element in improving quality in early childhood education is the professional development of educators working with children. This study aimed to analyze the needs, challenges, and opportunities of educators their professional development, based on their experiences and perceptions. The study employed a mixed-methods approach. Quantitative data were collected through a questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis Braun & Clarke (2021). The results indicate that educators consider professional development a factor for improving practices, yet they express a need for training in specific areas of their work. The qualitative analysis highlights challenges related to access to training, institutional conditions, support for professional growth, and the need for structured policies and mechanisms for continuous professional development. The findings offer implications for early childhood education policies and professional development programs at this educational level.

title: The Role of Educational and Training Strategies in Improving Service Quality in Tourism Businesses
abstract: This study aims to examine the role of educational strategies in improving service quality and their indirect impact on the demand for tourism business services in Kosovo. In this study, a quantitative research approach was used, and linear regression analysis was performed to assess the relationship between professional education and service quality. Therefore, in the first research model, service quality is treated as a dependent variable, while staff training and qualification, service standards, and customer feedback are considered mechanisms based on professional development and organizational learning. The findings show that staff training and qualification, and service standards positively and statistically significantly improve service quality, whereas customer feedback does not. In the second model, service demand was examined as an indirect result of education-driven quality improvement, with service promotion, advanced technology, modern infrastructure, and customer feedback included as independent variables. The results show that service promotion is a significant predictor of tourism demand. This study highlights the importance of continuing education, professional cap

title: Paul, Marschark, & Mayberry: An Integrated Perspective for Reading Development of D/Deaf and Hard of Hearing Students
abstract: The development of grade-level or age-level reading proficiency continues to be a challenge for a number of d/Deaf and hard of hearing (d/Dhh) children and adolescents. There have also been ongoing research debates on recommending evidence-based or effective practices to facilitate the acquisition of reading skills. These debates are fueled, in part, by the major principles of three broad frameworks: Paul’s Qualitative Similarity Hypothesis, Marschark’s Cognitive “Qualitative Difference” Hypothesis, and Mayberry’s L1-Timing Hypothesis. These frameworks highlight the tension between developmental similarity (continuity) and emerging neurocognitive reading research on d/Dhh individuals. The present commentary discusses the three frameworks, highlighting strengths and criticisms as well as similarities and differences, and concludes with a proposed integrative perspective with implications for classroom practices. This integration provides recommendations for further research, necessary for improving the reading levels of d/Deaf and hard of hearing students.

title: Cyberbullying Experiences Among Students with Disabilities: An Empirical Investigation
abstract: Cyberbullying represents a specific form of psychological violence that has intensified with the development of digital technology and the widespread use of social media. This study aims to analyze cyberbullying and its impact on students with disabilities in secondary education, considering them as a particularly vulnerable group. The research focuses on the forms in which cyberbullying manifests, the psychological, emotional, and social consequences it produces, as well as the factors contributing to its occurrence within the school context. The study also addresses strategies for preventing cyberbullying, emphasizing the roles of families, teachers, school psychologists, and educational institutions in creating a safe and inclusive school environment. Methodologically, the study is based on a mixed research approach, combining a review of relevant scientific literature with empirical research conducted through a questionnaire. Data were collected from a secondary school in the city of Gjilan, with 50 respondents participating from grades 10 to 12. The research underscores the need for coordinated and interdisciplinary approaches to address this phenomenon, which poses an increas

title: Psychological Dimensions of Organizational Culture in Healthcare Institutions
abstract: Organizational culture represents a complex system of shared values, professional beliefs, and behavioral patterns that shape employees’ cooperation, decision-making, and work performance within healthcare institutions. The quality of organizational culture directly influences employees’ motivation, job satisfaction, and readiness to accept changes in contemporary healthcare systems. This study examines the relationship between the psychological dimensions of organizational climate and employees’ innovation readiness in everyday professional practice. The research was conducted on a sample of 127 employees from different professional profiles working at the Health Center Zajecar. Data were collected using a questionnaire designed to assess organizational climate and employees’ innovation potential in healthcare institutions in Serbia. The results indicate that employees demonstrate readiness to accept new professional solutions; however, their implementation largely depends on organizational support, participative leadership, and available institutional resources. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening transformational leadership, improving internal communication, a

title: Teaching and Learning Practices in Multigrade Classes in Primary Education
abstract: This article aims to examine practices in multigrade teaching with a particular focus on how teachers model and plan learning content in multigrade classrooms and its relevance, as an important phenomenon in the schools of many European countries. Our study uses a qualitative model through semi-structured interviews and participatory classroom observations. Data sources include perceptions of 10 teachers serving in common classes 0-2 (preschool, first grade, and second grade), grades 3-4 (third and fourth grade), and 1- 4 (first, second, third, and fourth grade) in multigrade teaching in two Austrian primary schools. The results in this study show that integrated classes learn together in one classroom, while the curriculum is done as it should be done in separate classrooms, based on the level of the children and their needs. Among other things, this study demonstrates teaching models used in multigrade classrooms illustrated with examples of how teachers can apply learning content in different areas. in adapting integrated classrooms and how it can effectively support students’ individual learning.

title: Enhancing the Engagement of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder through Group-Based Interventions Utilizing the Social Robot NAO: A Synthetic Conceptual Analysis
abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (G-AI) and specifically Social Assistive Robotics (SARs) introduces innovative approaches in the field of education and especially in special education. This study is a synthetic conceptual analysis and examines key concepts around enhancing the engagement of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) in activities, focusing on group interventions utilizing the NAO robot by the teacher in the context of the classroom. The aim of this analysis is to clarify the definition and dimensions of engagement of children with ASD and to analyze the advantages of group interventions using the NAO as a teacher’s assistant. The results obtained highlight the associations between the characteristics of the NAO, the dimensions of engagement of children with ASD and the group intervention context. In addition, practical and theoretical implications are discussed, suggesting directions for future research in social robotics and its utilization in special education.

title: Behaviour Prevention of Stunting among the Indigenous People on The Coast of Bintan Island, Kepulauan Riau Province, Indonesia
abstract: The behaviour program demonstrates the potential of localized, culturally sensitive interventions in addressing public health issues in marginalized communities. The Suku Laut people are a marginalized community facing numerous health challenges, with stunting among children being a significant issue. This study focuses on the rantang sehat initiative, a targeted early intervention program aimed at preventing stunting within this vulnerable population. The research examines the effectiveness of the program, which provides nutritionally balanced meals to pregnant women, nursing mothers, and young children (Bayi Lima Tahun/Balita). The findings indicate a noticeable reduction in stunting prevalence among the children who participated in the program, highlighting the importance of consistent access to nutritious food during critical periods of growth. This study reveals the community’s perceptions of the program, noting an increase in awareness regarding the importance of nutrition for maternal and child health.

title: Professional Development and Training Needs of Vocational Rehabilitation Practitioners in Kosovo: A Comprehensive National Survey
abstract: Vocational rehabilitation (VR) practitioners in Kosovo operate within a developing post-conflict social support system, which requires strong professional accountability and evidence-based practice. Despite this need, formal certification systems and specialized training programs remain limited. This study provides the first comprehensive national assessment of the perceptions, practices, and professional development needs of VR practitioners in Kosovo, establishing baseline data to strengthen the national vocational rehabilitation framework. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among practitioners from public and non-public VR service providers across Kosovo’s seven regions between November 2023 and May 2024. The survey examined perceptions of research and training, current professional development activities, barriers to engagement, and preferences for training modalities. Out of 271 practitioners contacted, 142 completed the survey (52.4% response rate). The results showed that practitioners recognized the high utility of research (M=4.28, SD=0.75) and training (M=4.30, SD=0.70), but reported significant barriers including limited access to research guidance (M=2.45, SD

title: Tracheobronchial Foreign Bodies in Children: 67-year experience at ENT Clinic Tuzla
abstract: To evaluate clinical characteristics and outcomes of urgent bronchoscopies due to foreign body aspiration (FBA), we analyzed cases from January 1954 to December 2021. The study included children up to 14 years of age who underwent emergency bronchoscopy on suspicion of a foreign body in the lower respiratory tract. Each patient was assessed for age, sex, nature and location of the foreign body, bronchoscopy findings, complications, and airway involvement. A total of 889 children underwent urgent bronchoscopy over 67 years. Most cases (66.7%) occurred within the first three years of life, and 10.6% involved children under one year of age. Recently, a marked decrease in positive findings in infants has been observed. Boys represented 62.5% of cases. Organic foreign bodies, predominantly pumpkin seeds, were most common. The right bronchus was the predominant location (51%). In the most recent period, multiple-location foreign bodies became more frequent. Both the annual number of bronchoscopies and the proportion of positive findings have declined. During the COVID-19 pandemic, suspicion of FBA and the number of bronchoscopies significantly decreased.

title: Professional Development in the Educational Context - From Insecurity to Research Competence: Empowering Educators Through Research
abstract: The research, Experiences and Challenges in Implementing Action Research in Preschool Education, was conducted to analyze educators’ knowledge of research methods, to identify factors that influence their application, and to consider the possibilities of professional development and improving pedagogical practice. The results reveal challenges, awareness of research benefits, and motivation of employees for their application. Obstacles that arise during implementation relate to organizational issues, difficulty applying individualized approaches, inflexibility, and lack of institutional support. A negative trend is observed: as uncertainty increases, the level of perceived competence decreases. Spearman’s rank correlation and Kruskal-Wallis test confirm the negative relationship between uncertainty in applying research methods and the perception of their competence, and the analysis found that educators with higher self-assessed competence are more likely to implement research. The results indicate the need for systematic professional support to strengthen the identity of educators as reflective practitioners and researchers of practice.

title: Examining Teacher Educators’ Role in Enhancing Digital Competence in Vietnam’s Teacher Training Policies
abstract: Digital competence, which includes not only the capacity to utilize digital technologies but also the critical comprehension of digital environments, ethics, and pedagogy, has emerged as a fundamental component in the development of contemporary educational systems. Regarding Vietnam’s continuous efforts toward digital transformation, teacher educators bear a critical responsibility to prepare future teachers who can effectively navigate rapidly evolving educational and societal landscapes. The qualitative research investigates the roles and responsibilities assigned to teacher educators within Vietnam’s national teacher training. Through thematic analysis, the research identifies key themes related to examining the role of teacher educators in the advancement of digital competence in teacher education in Vietnamese policies. Professional engagement, digital resources, teaching and learning, the role of the teacher educator in fostering learners’ digital competencies, digital pedagogy, using digital tools, conceptual development, and transfer facilitation, which aids the aspiring teacher in navigating the digital teaching and learning environment, are the areas of inquiry. Findings

title: Cognitive Functioning, Anxiety, and Depression in Patients with Intracranial Tumors with and Without Aphasia
abstract: Introduction: Cognitive impairment is the most common neurological disorder associated with brain tumors, which leads to linguistic communication damage. Anxiety and depression are among the most prevalent psychiatric comorbidities in this population. Objectives: To determine the level of cognitive functioning, anxiety, and depression in patients with intracranial tumors with and without aphasia. Subjects and methods: A prospective study was conducted on 91 patients with verified brain tumors which were hospitalized at the Clinic for Neurosurgery for one year period. The patients were assessed with Mini Mental State Examination, Beck’s depression inventory, and Beck’s anxiety inventory. The type and severity of aphasia were determined by the Boston Aphasia Test. Results: The highest number of patients, a total of 31 (37.3%), had moderate anxiety disorder. 30 patients (36.1%) had shown symptoms of moderate depression, and 33 (39.7%) had shown mild and moderate cognitive dysfunction. Conclusion: Anxiety, depression, and cognitive dysfunction were significantly more pronounced in subjects with aphasia.

title: Investigation of Content Validity and Exploratory Factor Analysis of Students’ Pedagogical Knowledge of Science
abstract: This study aims to enhance the pedagogical knowledge of science among pre-service teachers in Elementary School Teacher Education (ESTE) and identify the factors influencing their understanding of scientific concepts. We employed Cohen’s Kappa coefficient to assess inter-rater reliability for the evaluation tools, alongside exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to uncover latent constructs related to Pedagogical Knowledge of Science (PKS) with a sample size of 989 pre-service science teachers in Elementary School Teacher Education (ESTE). questionnaire is designed to measure various dimensions of their pedagogical content knowledge. The findings indicate that Cohen’s Kappa coefficient demonstrated strong reliability at 0.8 across multiple items in the assessment tool, suggesting consistent agreement between raters. Furthermore, exploratory factor analysis (EFA) revealed an excellent model fit. PKS has 3 domains, namely Pedagogy of Science Curriculum (PoSC), Pedagogy of Science Instructional Strategies (PoSIS), and Pedagogy of Learner and Learning (PoLL). title: Cognitive Functions and Cross-Modal Plasticity in Children with Cochlear Implants: A Systematic Review of Research
abstract: This paper aims to systematically present existing research on cognitive and executive functions, speech and auditory perception, language, literacy, and academic development, and cross-modal reorganization in children with CIs. The methodology included a systematic search of databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) using keywords related to cognition and CIs. After eliminating duplicates and applying inclusion criteria, an analysis was conducted of relevant references published from 2015 to the present, which were analyzed both in tables and narratively. Research confirms that the cognitive development of children with CIs depends on auditory input and the brain’s ability to integrate information from different sensory modalities. Multisensory and interactive approaches to rehabilitation have the potential to enhance cognitive development and should be further researched and applied in practice.

title: Empowering Rural Education: A Transformative Approach Through Action Research, Innovative Pedagogy, And Technology Integration for Student Engagement and Achievement
abstract: This research article explores the implementation of action research as a transformative approach to enhance innovative teaching strategies in rural government schools. Recognizing the unique challenges faced in these contexts, the study investigates the integration of technology and community involvement to foster student engagement and improve learning outcomes. Utilizing a mixed-methods research design, data were collected through surveys, interviews, and classroom observations involving faculty and students. The findings reveal significant improvements in student participation and academic performance following the adoption of innovative practices, such as project-based learning and collaborative teaching methods. This study highlights the critical role of action research in facilitating continuous improvement in educational practices and offers actionable recommendations for educators and policymakers aimed at enriching the learning experience in rural settings. Key terms include action research, innovative teaching strategies, rural education, student engagement, and educational technology.

title: Exploring Number Sense in Students with Dyslexia, Dyscalculia, and Dysgraphia
abstract: This study examines number sense in students formally diagnosed with dyslexia, dyscalculia, and dysgraphia - specific learning difficulties that do not impact intelligence but affect reading, writing, and calculation. Five students completed a test of 33 tasks divided into six components that measure different aspects of number sense. The lowest performance was recorded in understanding the size and meaning of numbers (7%), while the best results were achieved in evaluating and comparing expressions without calculation (40%). Students were more successful when solving tasks set in an everyday context that allowed for assessment and logical reasoning, and did not require the technical execution of algorithms. The interviews further confirmed the importance of individual attention and support from teachers. These findings highlight the importance of functional, visually supported mathematics instruction, as well as systemic support for students with difficulties, in enabling them to learn mathematics in a more effective, meaningful, and motivating way.

title: Understanding the Self-Reported Reading Habits of Middle School Students with Dyslexia in Inclusive Classrooms in Türkiye
abstract: This study explored the reading habits of middle school students with dyslexia who participate in inclusive education in Türkiye. The sample included 77 students in grades 6–8 from diverse socioeconomic backgrounds. Data were collected using a demographic form and an adapted version of the Reading Habit Scale. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, and ANOVA were used for analysis. Results indicated that students generally reported moderate to high levels of reading habits. Significant differences were found based on gender, academic achievement, and participation in supplementary support education programs. No significant differences were observed for other demographic variables. Findings highlight the importance of individualized supports in inclusive settings to promote reading engagement in students with dyslexia.
